newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Transport Minister Mac Maharaj has unveiled a 1.2 billion rand plan to transform the major airports at Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban over five years, and to develop dormant land adjacent to airports around South Afrcia.
- JCI mine Randfontein Estates is considering retrenching about 4,000 miners -- one third of its workforce -- in the wake of a declining gold price, lower ore grade and management problems.

- New Nation, one of the last bastions of the alternative media, will close on Friday after 10 years, following major losses in the past six months. Key editorial and management staff will be redeployed to the Sowetan.

- Amalgamated Banks of South Africa reported an increase of 28.6 percent to 1.32 billion rand in headline earnings in the year to March despite a poor second half which saw margins under pressure and consumers battle with high interest rates.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Mzi Khumalo, chairman of JCI, is to acquire NK Properties, the listed property loan stock company, to house his mining interests, sources said.
- New Age Beverages, Pepsi's bottler, halted operations on Monday after its application for voluntary liquidation on Friday.
- Illovo Sugar is to list on the Swazi stock exchange in the place of recently-acquired Lonrho Sugar.
- Amalgamated Banks of South Africa could announce the acquisition of an offshore private banking operation within the next two or three weeks.
- Randfontein Estates may retrench as many as 8,000 workers, according to the National Union of Mineworkers.
- Foreign direct investment commitments into South Africa have topped 31.6 billion rand since the 1994 lections, the BusinessMap consultancy said.
THE STAR
- Five people, including two sisters, burnt to death when two cars crashed when one of the drivers tried to avoid a pool of water as heavy stroms lashed the Reef on Monday.
- The South African Police Service is a sleeping giant which needs only to use its available resources effectively to win the war against crime, says newly appointed SAPS chief executive Meyer Kahn.
- Hundreds of Gauteng's young people will soon pour their time and labour into a provincial educational project that will see 50 schools being pugraded.

- The weekly newspaper New Nation announced its closure on Monday and said the final edition would appear on Friday. The chairman of New Africa Publications Limited Nthato Motlana said the paper, whose circulation had grown from 15,000 to 22,000 in the past two years, had continued to make a loss which could no longer be absorbed by shareholders.
- An overworked Deputy Presdient Thabo Mbeki, who has taken over most of the day-to-day running of the government from President Nelson Mandela, has decided to take a break.

- Police in Zimbabwe say two white South Africans were picked up for questioning about a suspected plot to assassinate presidents Nelson Mandela and Robert Mugabe during Mandela's state visit to Zimbabwe last week.
